audience_contract.primary: compiler engineers touching the AscendNPU-IR regbase/membase pipeline story who need to know when reshapes move, which option set they inherited, and why a propagation was refused
audience_contract.assumed_background: MLIR basics (tensor/memref reshape ops, reassociation indices, greedy rewrite drivers), no prior knowledge of this pass assumed

mental_model: The pass treats a tensor reshape as a movable barrier: instead of letting an elementwise or shape-like op work on a reshaped view, it slides collapse_shape toward the function's outputs and expand_shape toward the producers, so surrounding ops see the rank that matches their math. One pattern family per direction, an expand/collapse pair swap to unlock deadlocked orders, and a per-mode option set that changes not only thresholds but which moves across region boundaries are even attempted.
need: After conversion and canonicalization, IR mixes ops of different ranks connected by reshape ops: linalg/HFusion elemwise chains sit behind collapse_shape, and HIVM conversions insert reshape ops because HIVM brc/reduce demand same-rank operands. Downstream whole-function analyses (the Tidy/registerBased Flattener via DimensionAnalyzer) and vectorization need that reshape noise organized first — collapses pushed to the end, expands pushed upstream — otherwise the flattener either bails (hasUnpropagateableCase) or computes on a needlessly mixed-rank graph.
responsibility: Inside one func::FuncOp, run an option-shaped set of greedy rewrite patterns that move tensor/memref collapse_shape and expand_shape ops across a curated set of producer/consumer ops (elementwise, broadcast/reduce, transpose, interleave/deinterleave, slices, concat/pad, HIVM elemwise/brc/reduce, scf.for via PropagatableScfFor), swapping collapse-expand pairs when reassociations allow, while refusing every move that would change element order or break the fixpoint.
observable_outcome: Same values, different shape placement: elemwise ops operate at high rank with reshapes only at the boundaries (mulext test: both operands get the high-rank source and a fresh collapse_shape is emitted on the result); under forRegbased a flip migrates to expanded rank while a shared low-rank result is preserved with a new collapse; unit-dim expands under a set threshold stay put and the reduce/slice consumes the low-rank tensor instead. Functions that match no gate are returned unchanged; AIC functions and (under forRegbased+skipScope) scope-containing functions are never touched.

upstream.role: reshape producers at HIVM conversion time
upstream.interaction: Because HIVM brc/reduce operands must share rank, the conversions insert reshape ops that this pass must then re-propagate — the stated reason both forHIVM placements exist (placement d/e comment)

upstream.role: immediately preceding cleanup in the HFusion pipelines
upstream.entity: canonicalizationPipeline, LinalgFoldUnitExtentDims, ComposeMultiReduce, optional symbol propagation
upstream.interaction: preFlattenPass runs canonicalization and multi-reduce composition first so propagate-reshape sees a canonical tensor graph; propagate-reshape then runs before one more SimplifyOps + canonicalization round

upstream.role: elementwise + reshape mix from frontends and earlier lowering
upstream.interaction: produces the elemwise-behind-reshape pattern the pass description targets; canonicalization patterns of collapse/expand are re-registered inside the pass's own pattern set so folding and propagation interleave in one greedy sweep

downstream.interaction: in both forRegbased placements the pass runs immediately before FoldTensorEmpty + CanonicalizeTensorReshape + canonicalization + FlattenOps; the flattener analyzes the entire function and bails on unpropagateable cases, so the reshape layout this pass establishes is its starting position

the forHIVM placement runs at the head of this pipeline (followed by RemoveRedundantLoopInit, NormalizeMatmul, InsertFixpipe, …), giving bufferization a graph where brc/reduce reshapes have been pushed to their natural ends
runs after the HFusion flatten block (buildHFusionRegBasePipeline ends with it), so vectorization consumes the flattened, propagation-normalized shapes

triggers.entity: buildHFusionPipelines / buildHFusionRegBasePipeline / buildConvertToHIVMPipeline / buildHIVMTensorOptimizations (regbase and non-regbase variants), wired by bishengir-compile
triggers.interaction: each decides independently whether to insert the pass and with which option shape (default, forRegbased, or forHIVM), based on enableFlatten, enableTritonKernelCompile, enableMixedCV and hacc::utils::isRegBasedArch(target)

inputs.name: func.func body (tensor form)
inputs.form: ranked tensor SSA graph containing tensor.collapse_shape / tensor.expand_shape (and, for the memref companions, their memref counterparts) with producer/consumer ops from linalg, hfusion, hivm, tensor, scf
inputs.description: operates on the whole function; AIC-labeled functions and scope-containing functions (regbase mode) are filtered out before pattern application

inputs.name: PropagateReshapeOptions
inputs.form: forHIVM=false, forRegbased=false, skipScope=true, maxUnitDimsForPropagation=10 by default; set per placement
inputs.description: the option triple selects pattern membership, region-boundary policy, unit-dim thresholds and the skip gate

outputs.name: rewritten function (or unchanged)
outputs.form: same function, reshapes relocated: collapses adjacent to function outputs/ends, expands adjacent to producers, expand-collapse pairs swapped to a common refinement, elemwise/brc/reduce/flip ops operating at the rank that matches their math
outputs.description: original reshapes are replaced (replaceAllUsesWith) by newly created collapse/expand ops at the moved positions; a failing greedy rewrite signals pass failure instead of emitting invalid IR

mechanism.summary: Per function: gate, assemble an option-dependent pattern set, and run one greedy rewrite sweep in which four pattern families (collapse-down, expand-up, collapse/expand swap, near-end expand-down) plus canonicalizers drive reshapes to their mode-preferred positions until a fixpoint.

stages.name: Function-level skip gate
stages.what: build the options struct from the pass flags; return untouched if the function is AIC-labeled (queryFuncCoreType) or — only in regbase mode with skipScope — contains a scope.scope op

stages.name: Option-dependent pattern assembly
stages.what: register the i1-cast collapse pattern, the four tensor/memref canonicalizers, SwapCollapseExpand, PropagateExpandUp, PropagateCollapseDown, the memref propagate pair, plus PropagateNearEndExpandDown and memref::SwapMemrefCollapseExpand only outside regbase mode

stages.name: Greedy rewrite to fixpoint
stages.what: applyPatternsGreedily over the function; any pattern failure inside the driver signals pass failure (signalPassFailure) rather than silently continuing

stages.name: Collapse-down propagation
stages.what: for each tensor.collapse_shape with a non-stop-propagatable defining op, walk its users and dispatch by op kind (store, materialize-in-destination, mulext, annotation mark, arange, bitcast, concat, pad, broadcast, reduce-like, slices, elementwise, flip, transpose, interleave/deinterleave, HIVM elemwise/brc/reduce, extract): rebind the user to the high-rank source and re-create a collapse on the user's result; DPS ops without pure tensor semantics and unhandled kinds are left alone

stages.name: Expand-up propagation
stages.what: for each tensor.expand_shape, inspect its defining op and dispatch through the same op families (plus scf::ForOp via PropagatableScfFor): recreate the producer at expanded rank and collapse back at the boundary; entry guards enforce stop-propagatability, out-only users, cross-region policy, the forHIVM non-unit requirement and the forRegbased unit-dim threshold

stages.name: Collapse/expand swap
stages.what: rewrite expand(collapse(x)) by computing fixed then loose reassociation compatibility to a common refinement shape, then placing a new expand on the collapse source and a new collapse reproducing the original result — unlocking the orders the two directional patterns cannot move directly

stages.name: Near-end expand-down (non-regbase only)
stages.what: when every user of an expand is the expand itself, a return, or an elemwise store/copy/load chain with a single DPS input, push the expand past those final elemwise users toward the end of the function — registered only when NOT forRegbased

control_flow: pipeline builders (option shape chosen by isRegBasedArch/enableFlatten/enableTritonKernelCompile) drive the pass, which never calls other passes
inside the pass, runOnOperation drives one greedy rewrite driver; the driver chooses pattern application order by benefit, so the four families interleave rather than run in phases
data_flow: value identity is preserved end-to-end: patterns rewrite operand wiring and re-create collapse/expand wrappers around unchanged compute ops (updateDefiningOp + expandAndReplace/collapseAndReplace)

the only 'data' that moves is rank: an op's operands/results are re-typed between the reshaped and unreshaped shapes, with reassociation indices recomputed (renumberReassociation, dim inc/dec helpers)

provenance.source: bishengir/test/Dialect/Tensor/propagate-reshape-a5-regbase.mlir @ HEAD 90037fe3 (checked-in FileCheck expectations, read but NOT executed; runtime_verification none)

canonical_example.initial_state: func.func @flip_expand(%arg0: tensor<2x12x5xf32>): hfusion.flip at low rank (flip_axis=2) → tensor.expand_shape [[0],[1,2],[3]] → math.absf at tensor<2x3x4x5xf32>, with the low-rank flipped value also returned
canonical_example.inputs: the same .mlir run twice by the test harness with -propagate-reshape="for-regbased=false" (A3 prefix) and "for-regbased=true" (REGBASE prefix)
execution_trace: REGBASE: PropagateExpandUp crosses hfusion.flip (FlipOp handling is regbase-only): the expand moves above the flip, which now flips axis 3 of tensor<2x3x4x5xf32>

REGBASE: because %flipped still has a second (low-rank) user — the return — a new tensor.collapse_shape is created on the moved flip's result to preserve that user (shared users pin their own collapse)
A3: with for-regbased=false the FlipOp dispatch does not exist, so the flip stays below/above as written and only the expand/collapse canonicalizations apply

counter-example in the same file: flip_collapse_reject_group_axis keeps the flip at low rank in BOTH modes — a flip axis spanning a reassociation group ([1,2]) would reorder elements inside the group, so the move is refused
canonical_example.result: REGBASE expects expand → flip(axis=3) → collapse(low-rank) → return; A3 expects flip(axis=2, low rank) → expand → return — identical math, different shape ownership

decisions.question: Which functions does the pass process at all?
decisions.condition: queryFuncCoreType(f) == hivm::TFuncCoreType::AIC, or (forRegbased && skipScope && the function contains a scope.scope op)
outcomes: AIC function → return immediately, no rewrite (cube-side code is out of scope)
regbase mode + scope op present → return immediately, no rewrite
otherwise → proceed to pattern application (note: with default options skipScope has no effect because the guard is conjunct with forRegbased)
decisions.reason: cube functions and scope-structured regbase functions have shape semantics this pass's analysis does not model; skipping is cheaper and safer than partial legality

decisions.question: Which pattern families are assembled for this run?
outcomes: regbase: no PropagateNearEndExpandDown, no memref::SwapMemrefCollapseExpand — the pattern set is the regbase subset
non-regbase: full set including the near-end expand-down and the memref swap
decisions.reason: regbase mode replaces the A3-era near-end/memref behaviors with its own cross-region and batch-processing policy instead of adding on top

decisions.question: Which mode's dispatch table applies to a reshape's neighbor op?
decisions.condition: forRegbased vs forHIVM vs default, evaluated per candidate op
outcomes: hfusion::FlipOp and tensor::ExtractOp (expand-up) and bufferization::MaterializeInDestinationOp are crossed only under forRegbased
tensor::ExtractSliceOp/InsertSliceOp are crossed only when NOT forHIVM
linalg::FillOp expand-up is refused under forRegbased (documented non-termination interaction with collapse-down via concat/extract_slice chains)
VReduceOp/ReduceWithIndexOp argmin-argmax-style second results block propagation unless forRegbased
decisions.reason: each mode has different correctness and fixpoint constraints: regbase adds reg-local ops and stricter fixpoint protection, HIVM mode excludes slice forms its conversions re-generate

decisions.question: Does a reshape cross a region boundary?
decisions.condition: candidate op's parent region differs, and mode: allowed only when forRegbased AND the reshape/defining result has exactly one use
outcomes: regbase + single use → the move crosses the boundary (A5 policy)
multiple users or non-regbase → stay inside the region (A3 policy: never move shared producers across regions)
decisions.reason: moving a multi-use producer across a region would duplicate or strand uses; regbase permits exactly the single-use case and then processes all snapshotted users together so the greedy driver makes monotonic progress

decisions.question: Is a candidate shape too unit-dim-heavy to propagate?
decisions.condition: forRegbased && llvm::count(shape, 1) > maxUnitDimsForPropagation (default 10), checked on the collapse source (collapse-down), expand result (expand-up) and the swap's common refinement
outcomes: exceeds threshold → match failure, the reshape stays where it is
decisions.reason: the FIXME-documented hazard: unit dims can be re-propagated endlessly without changing element count, so rank is unbounded by shape factorization; the threshold is an explicit temporary termination safeguard introduced by commit 92a45873b

decisions.question: Which pipeline placement and option shape does this compile use?
decisions.condition: target reg-based? flatten enabled? Triton kernel compile? regbase HIVM pipe?
outcomes: reg-based target + enableFlatten → forRegbased variant immediately before FlattenOps (placements b, c)
any HFusion pipeline pre-flatten stage → default options (placements a, and the membase twin)

target NOT reg-based → forHIVM variant right after ConvertToHIVM and in the pre-bufferization pipeline (placements d, e; enableRegBaseHIVMPipe is isRegBasedArch(target)) — i.e. both HIVM-side regbase-file placements are skipped when the target IS reg-based
membase Triton branch → forHIVM variant in buildHFusionPipelines (non-regbase file)
decisions.reason: the same reshape problem appears at three different representation boundaries (HFusion pre-flatten, post-HIVM-conversion, pre-bufferization), and each boundary needs a different option shape; the regbase story deliberately re-derives shapes via FlattenOps instead of re-running HIVM-mode propagation

constraints.statement: Propagation must preserve element order and count: flip axes spanning a reassociation group are refused in every mode because the move would reorder elements inside the group
A reshape's source/defining op must exist and must not be stop-propagatable (isInitOp or arith::ConstantOp); reshapes rooted at constants or function inits never move

The greedy driver must reach a fixed point; the pass explicitly refuses the expand-up-over-fill move under regbase because it documented non-termination interacting with collapse-down through concat/extract_slice chains

Rank growth under unit-dim propagation is not bounded by shape factorization; maxUnitDimsForPropagation (default 10) is a declared temporary termination safeguard, to be replaced by a semantic condition
DPS ops without pure tensor semantics and ops the dispatch does not recognize (including hivm::VTransposeOp, a marked TODO) are left untouched rather than partially rewritten

invariants.statement: All rewrites keep the function's external behavior: moved reshapes are view-like ops, and every replaced reshape's users are re-bound to a newly created collapse/expand that reproduces the original type
Shared users are honored: when a reshaped value has multiple users, propagation re-binds only the propagatable user(s) and keeps/emits a collapse for the others (mulext shared-user test)
The pass is per-function and stateless between functions: every decision derives from the options struct fixed at construction plus local IR inspection

boundaries.statement: Crossing elementwise (marked and HIVM nary), linalg broadcast/reduce/transpose, hfusion flip/interleave/deinterleave/mulext/reduce-with-index, tensor concat/pad/extract, slices (mode-gated), HIVM brc/reduce/copy/store/load/bitcast, scf.for (expand-up), and annotation marks
scf.for propagation exists only on the expand-up side via PropagatableScfFor; the collapse-down side has no corresponding handler in the dispatch

Moves that change element order (flip over a reassociation group), expand-up over linalg.fill under regbase (fixpoint hazard), propagation into AIC functions and scope-containing functions in regbase mode, and reshapes rooted at constants/inits

The unit-dim threshold is an admitted stopgap: a shape above the default threshold silently stops propagating, so behavioral differences between modes (test shows DEFAULT vs REGBASE giving opposite shape ownership) are option-dependent by design
No handler for func.call/return-boundary propagation appears in either dispatch; whether reshape propagation across function boundaries is handled elsewhere was not determined from the files read

placement.why_here: It sits at the last moments where shapes are still explicit tensor reshapes: before the Tidy/registerBased Flattener consumes the whole function's shape structure (regbase flatten placements), and immediately after HIVM conversion / before bufferization where conversions themselves insert reshapes (forHIVM placements). Canonicalizers run right before it, and FoldTensorEmpty + CanonicalizeTensorReshape + canonicalization run right after, so it works on a canonical graph and hands a normalized one onward.
placement.why_not_earlier: Earlier, the graph still contains multi-reduce compositions, uncanonicalized slices and (on the HIVM side) hasn't been converted yet — the reshapes it propagates (especially the conversion-inserted brc/reduce reshapes) do not exist until those steps run.
placement.why_not_later: After FlattenOps/AutoVectorizeV2 the explicit reshape structure is gone (shapes are flattened/vectorized), and after bufferization reshapes become memref views where this tensor-level analysis no longer applies; the memref companion patterns exist precisely as the late-stage fallback within the same pass.
placement.status: derived from placement code and surrounding pass order

ownership.shared: legality helpers (isStopPropagatable/isOutOp) live in bishengir/lib/Dialect/Utils/Util.cpp and are shared with HFusion reshape utilities; memref pattern implementations live under bishengir/lib/Dialect/MemRef/Transforms/PropagateReshape/

complexity.pattern_count: 7 pattern families in the driver (4 tensor-level + 2 memref propagate + memref swap), ~5.3k lines across the PropagateReshape directory (measured with wc -l)
complexity.dispatch_breadth: the two directional patterns each dispatch over ~20 op kinds with per-mode gates
complexity.provenance: derived (line counts and dispatch cases counted from source at HEAD)

key_takeaways: propagate-reshape moves reshapes, not data: collapse_shape slides toward function outputs, expand_shape toward producers, so consumers do math at their natural rank — and the original reshape is always replaced by a fresh pair that reproduces each user's type

forRegbased/forHIVM are not tuning knobs but mode switches that change the pattern set, the region-boundary policy (A3 one-at-a-time + no cross-region vs A5 single-use cross-region + batch users), and the dispatch table itself

the regbase story is conditional: with a reg-based target the pass runs (only if flatten is enabled) before FlattenOps, while BOTH HIVM-file placements are skipped exactly when the target is reg-based — they exist to clean up conversion-inserted reshapes on the non-regbased path

legality is mostly about element order and termination: flip-over-group rejections and the FIXME-documented unit-dim threshold (default 10) show the pass defends the fixpoint, and the fill rejection proves non-termination was a real occurrence
it is a pre-analysis normalizer: its value is measured by what FlattenOps, bufferization and vectorization receive — organized reshape boundaries — not by any performance claim of its own

pass.pass_arg: bishengir-opt --propagate-reshape (defaults: for-hivm=false, for-regbased=false, skip-scope=true, max-unit-dims-for-propagation=10); mode examples from the tests: --propagate-reshape="for-regbased=true max-unit-dims-for-propagation=6", --propagate-reshape="for-regbased=false"
pass.operation_scope: func::FuncOp (tablegen pass scope); whole-function greedy rewrite; AIC functions and (forRegbased+skipScope) scope-containing functions are excluded; no module-level or region-level entry

ir_contract.before: a func.func where tensor.collapse_shape / tensor.expand_shape (and memref twins) sit between producers and consumers of different ranks: e.g. elemwise ops reading a collapsed view (mulext test: elemwise_binary → collapse_shape → mulext at tensor<6x4xi32>), or flips/reduces/slices consuming reshaped values
ir_contract.after: reshapes relocated to the boundary: the mulext case becomes elemwise_binary → mulext at tensor<2x3x4xi32> → collapse_shape back to tensor<6x4xi32> per user; the regbase flip case becomes expand_shape → flip at expanded rank → collapse_shape for the low-rank user; collapse-expand pairs may be re-associated onto a common refinement shape; untouched ops keep their exact types
ir_contract.element_preservation: element count and order are preserved in every rewrite; moves that could reorder (flip over a reassociation group) are refused in all modes

legality: source/defining op must exist and not be stop-propagatable (isInitOp || arith::ConstantOp)
reassociation compatibility: swap requires fixed then loose reassociation agreement on a common refinement shape
element order: flips only move when their axis maps to a single source dimension inside the reassociation group
cross-region moves: only forRegbased and only for single-use values
unit-dim budget: forRegbased rejects shapes with more than maxUnitDimsForPropagation (default 10) unit dims

fixpoint protection: expand-up over linalg.fill refused under forRegbased; argmin/argmax-style second results block reduce propagation unless forRegbased; DPS ops without pure tensor semantics skipped
if applyPatternsGreedily still fails, the pass signals failure rather than emitting the intermediate state
pass.rewrite: Greedy pattern rewrite with no separate analysis: each match rebinds operands (updateDefiningOp / updateDefiningOpNonDst), re-creates reshapes at the moved position via shared utilities (expandAndReplace / collapseAndReplace / createNewReshapingOp, renumberReassociation and the dim inc/dec reassociation helpers), and replaces the old reshape's uses; the swap pattern replaces expand(collapse(x)) with a new pair on the common refinement; all creations are plain rewrites so the driver owns convergence
